title: Celebrating SG Families: Embracing Parenthood through Live, Work and Play
what_it_is: Celebrating SG Families: Embracing Parenthood through Live, Work and Play

sections.label: Family support efforts in Singapore
sections.summary: Efforts include the National Family Council, now Families for Life, family-oriented resources, 2022 as a year celebrating families, and the launch of A Singapore Made for Families 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Much effort has been made accordingly throughout the years in this aspect, such as the formation of the National Family Council, now known as Families for Life, and the introduction of family-oriented resources, including the parenting workshops and symposiums.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This endeavour continues today, as 2022 has been dedicated as a year in celebration of families in Singapore and the plan of "A Singapore Made for Families 2025", or "MFF 2025" in short, was launched recently as the Government's plan for creating a Singapore that values and supports family well-being.

sections.label: Preschool places and rental suggestions
sections.summary: The bottleneck is a lack of preschool childcare slots; 22,000 full-day places will be created, and ECDA is urged to help anchor operators rent premises near transport nodes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Based on the two examples that I have just shared, the main bottleneck seems to be in the lack of available slots in preschool childcare, especially for infant care and playgroup sessions, particularly in areas with more young families where demand has grown over the COVID-19 period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, I am heartened to learn about the recent Government announcement that an additional 22,000 full-day preschool places will be created over the next two years, of which, 2,800 places will be set aside for infant care and 4,400 for playgroup programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In relation to this Government offering more resources in this aspect, I hope to make the following suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I hope that ECDA can also consider encouraging the five anchor preschool operators to rent more premises near MRT and bus interchanges by appealing for and facilitating subsidised rental rates with Government support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is akin to the concept behind the 21,500 square feet Space @ Woods Square that was donated by the developers of an integrated commercial development, with the aim of providing new community space in Woodlands, bringing together three non-profit organisations, such as the Care Corner Singapore, New Life Community Services and World Vision Singapore, so that they can more effectively partner and help Singaporeans in need who live in the northern part of the country.

sections.label: PCF Cashew Centre childcare spaces
sections.summary: PCF's Cashew Centre in Hillion Mall offers full-day childcare and infant care for up to 287 children, and PCF announced 2,500 more preschool spaces by end of next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Its Cashew Centre, which is situated in Hillion Mall, spreads over 21,500 square feet, offering high-quality and accessible full-day childcare and infant care services for up to 287 children, ranging from the age of two months to six years old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Recently, PCF has further announced that another 2,500 preschool spaces will be added by the end of next year.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements article
sections.summary: A Straits Times article highlighted pros and cons of flexible work arrangements, and the speaker urges employers and employees to explore hybrid work under the Tripartite Standard on FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In fact, in the recent Straits Times article titled "Making Flexible Arrangements Work", both the pros and cons of flexible work arrangements were highlighted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It would, therefore, make sense, and I urge more employers and employees to better understand each other's needs and concerns and explore whether a hybrid work arrangement by adopting the Tripartite Standard on Flexible Work Arrangements (FWAs) is viable, with a common view towards achieving a goal-oriented approach, in the interest of maximising productivity.

sections.label: Reintroducing SingapoRediscovers Vouchers
sections.summary: Residents could afford local attractions thanks to SingapoRediscovers Vouchers, and the speaker proposes reintroducing the vouchers to encourage family bonding in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   The usual prices for admission tickets to some local attractions were usually out of the budget for some families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, in the recent two years, several of my residents have informed me that they were, finally, able to afford them, thanks to the SingapoRediscovers Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As such, to consider offering another round of such concessions will likely be well-received by Singaporeans, especially those families with young children and grandparents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, propose that the Government and the Community work together again to reintroduce the vouchers in some capacity, branding it as an initiative to encourage family bonding in Singapore.

sections.label: Free Sunday admissions to attractions
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for free Sunday admissions to selected local attractions such as the Zoo, museums and Gardens by the Bay, apart from incentive vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For a start in Singapore, apart from the introduction of incentive vouchers, I hope we can have free Sunday admissions to selected local attractions, such as the Zoo, museums, Gardens by the Bay and so on.

sections.label: Review of family-related policies
sections.summary: The speaker believes now is the right time for stakeholders to review family-related policies, regulations and family-friendly work practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With the easing of safety measures and with our country now embarking on Forward SG conversations, consulting and planning for the next 50 years and beyond, I believe it is now the right opportunity for all relevant stakeholders to review existing family-related policies, regulations and family-friendly work practices moving forward so as to build more support networks and resilience among Singaporeans, their families and the business community.

sections.label: Increase in preschool places
sections.summary: Over five years, infant care places rose about 60% to over 12,000 and childcare places rose 35% to 195,000, with 22,000 more announced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Over the last five years, we have increased the national supply of preschool places significantly – infant care places by around 60%, from 7,500 places in 2017 to over 12,000 places today, and childcare places by 35%, from 143,000 places in 2017 to 195,000 places.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As Ms Hany Soh shared, Minister Masagos Zulkifli had recently announced an expansion of another 22,000 places over the next two years, including about 2,800 places and 4,400 places set aside for infant care and playgroups respectively.

sections.label: More early childhood educators needed
sections.summary: Early childhood educators rose from 18,000 in 2018 to over 23,000 in 2021, but about 3,500 more are needed by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Despite the number of early childhood educators increasing steadily from 18,000 in 2018 to over 23,000 in 2021, the workforce will require about 3,500 more educators by 2025 to meet the demands of the growing number of preschool places in Singapore.

sections.label: Families for Life family-friendly practices
sections.summary: Families for Life works with trade associations and companies to champion family-friendly workplace practices, with the Made For Families brand mark and Great Companies for Dads Awards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Families for Life (FFL), the national movement to strengthen and support families, has also been working closely with trade associations and companies to champion family-friendly practices in the workplace, such as leaving work early for Eat With Your Family days, something that was also highlighted by Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat yesterday.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Companies with family-friendly programmes are encouraged to adopt the Made For Families brand mark and are recognised through the Centre for Fathering's annual "Great Companies for Dads Awards".

sections.label: Made for Families 2025 events
sections.summary: Under the Made for Families 2025 plan, Families for Life will work with partners to organise events such as family picnics and family days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As part of the Made for Families 2025 plan, Families for Life will also be working with partners to organise events, such as family picnics and family days.
